brief:
According to Al Jazeera English, Israeli military personnel deployed to Gaza are experiencing profound psychological distress, described as "Gaza Syndrome," stemming from their involvement in the conflict. The soldiers are confronting lasting trauma related to operations conducted during the war, with mental health consequences extending beyond the battlefield into their civilian lives.

The psychological toll reflects broader impacts of the conflict on those involved in combat operations. Mental health professionals and military officials have begun documenting the scale of trauma among returning troops, raising concerns about long-term care and rehabilitation needs for affected soldiers and their families.
dek: The trauma Israeli soldiers bring home — and the consequences of Israel’s genocide in Gaza.
title: Israeli soldiers return from Gaza suffering severe trauma and psychological damage
